Recognize the approach

Glassmorphism uses translucent, blurred surfaces to imply depth.

Look for

  • Blurred backdrop
  • Translucent surface layers
  • Fine edges and controlled highlights

Your learning goal

Describe the visual decisions before choosing a tool. Then make one small example that uses them deliberately.

Next: Origins

Where it comes from

Glassmorphism uses translucent, blurred surfaces to imply depth. Earlier interfaces used related effects; the modern label describes a treatment that can coexist with many layout styles.

Period or influence
2020s label; earlier translucent UI precedents
What this label describes

What to examine

Look at the heading, one control, the image treatment, and the reading order. Explain which decisions establish the style and which make the page usable.

Next: Construction

How to construct it

  1. Use backdrop-filter with a sufficiently opaque background and a solid fallback.
  2. Test text over every part of the underlying image. Keep menus and reading panels opaque when transparency hurts clarity.

Small practice task

Place one panel over two different backgrounds. Increase its opacity until both versions remain easy to read.

Before you expand it

Test the result at its intended size, on a narrow screen, and with keyboard focus. Preserve editable layers and record the source and license of acquired assets.
